headline: Every can checked, not a sample.
label: #F7E9D2
visitLine: Call and visit to Emu Plains
heroLede: Mountain Culture has run its own canning line from the start, and its Emu Plains brewery was built to lift capacity from two million to eight million litres a year. With a steady stream of limited releases, a different beer can be on the line every few days. This is what a camera check could look like on your can line. Scroll through, then adjust the estimate at the end to your own numbers.
lidLede: The camera checks every can has its end on and seated, with no visible damage around the seam. It looks at what can be seen from outside, so it adds to your seam checks rather than replacing them.
labelLede: With new releases going through all the time, the wrong label on a run is an easy mistake. The camera checks every can carries the right label for the beer inside, straight and intact.
codeLede: Fresh, hoppy beer is all about the date. The system reads the printed best-before and batch code on every can and compares them with the beer and date set at changeover.
objectLede: Can ends, label backing and carton offcuts can all end up on the conveyor. The camera over the belt spots anything that should not be there before it reaches a carton.

vocab.alert: Four ends not seated in fifteen minutes. Check the seamer.
